core_obligations: Observe that a countable directed set has a cofinal subset isomorphic to (N, >=) (proof lines 2436-2437).
Use cofinality to turn a presentation indexed by a countable Lambda into a sequence of thickenings of affine schemes, which gives (2) implies (1) (proof line 2437).
Conversely read a sequential presentation as one indexed by the countable directed set N, which gives (1) implies (2) (proof line 2437).
difficulty_reason: For an affine formal algebraic space X over S, the lemma states the equivalence of two conditions: that X be the colimit of a sequence X_1 -> X_2 -> ... of thickenings of affine schemes, and that X admit a presentation X = colim X_lambda with Lambda countable (statement lines 2422-2433). The proof records the point that makes the two conditions the same: a countable directed set has a cofinal subset isomorphic to (N, >=), so any countable presentation can be reindexed as a sequence and conversely (proof lines 2435-2438). The level is H2: the equivalence is short, but the passage between the two indexings is exactly what has to be observed, and it is stated with the cofinality reason.
